clue.text: A lot of women rush to get married

parts.note: to hare is to rush or run fast

explanation.surface: Lots of women hurry to the altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the group of wives and concubines in a household, so a whole lot of women together.

clue.text: Ambassador naive but cruel

parts.note: HE is His (or Her) Excellency, the title of an ambassador
artless means naive, without guile

explanation.surface: An envoy who is innocent yet unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without a heart, figuratively, has no pity and so is cruel.

clue.text: Cabinet moves to get a new deal

definitions.meaning: a government's changing of ministers between posts
shuffling a pack of cards again before dealing

explanation.surface: Ministers being moved around in search of a fresh deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime minister's rearrangement of ministers has this name, and so does mixing the playing cards over again.

clue.text: A parent sober and dull

parts.note: ma is a mother, one parent
TT means teetotal, so sober

explanation.surface: A mother who is teetotal and boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A matt finish is dull, without gloss or shine.

clue.text: Newly-wed hale and hearty in prison

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married
well means in good health

explanation.surface: A healthy new bride is somehow behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridewell was a London prison, and the name came to mean any house of correction.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell, originally a London house of correction, became a general term for a jail.

clue.text: If you are Mr Maxwell's nephew, everything's fine!

definitions.text: If you are Mr Maxwell's nephew
definitions.meaning: the press baron Robert Maxwell was known as Bob, so his nephew would literally have Bob as uncle
a British catchphrase meaning all is sorted, there you are

explanation.surface: A family connection to the tycoon guarantees all will be well.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase means there you go, job done; taken literally it describes a nephew of anyone called Bob.

clue.text: Vital backing, yet it's not good

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for vital is read from its end to its start

parts.note: live means living, full of life, so vital

explanation.surface: Something essential runs in reverse, and that is bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness is the opposite of goodness, so the bad is the evil.

clue.text: Respond to the final cry of one feeling the pinch!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Respond to the final cry of one feeling the pinch!': END + OW gives the letters, but 'Respond' cannot define a word meaning 'provide'; likely an OCR misread of the definition, no scan available.
annotationWithheld.clue: Respond to the final cry of one feeling the pinch!

clue.text: Comparatively humble, but neat

definitions.meaning: more humble, less high in rank
an old word for cattle, the beasts that moo

explanation.surface: Something both humbler and tidier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for cattle, and a cow is one that lows.
explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is lesser in rank; the other is an animal that lows, as cattle do.

clue.text: Adjustable seats prove an advantage

indicators.note: seats that can be adjusted are rearranged, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Car seats that adjust turn out to be a selling point.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, a benefit.

clue.text: Dog taken round an Indian bay

indicators.note: the word for a dog is wrapped around the abbreviation

parts.note: bow-wow is a child's word for a dog
IND is an abbreviation for Indian

explanation.surface: A dog led around an Indian bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' reads as a stretch of coast or a horse's colour; it is the window.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay is a window projecting outward from a wall, often curved.

clue.text: Midland town map-lover disposed to take Henry to heart

indicators.note: with the following words, says the letters swallow the next piece into their middle
into the very centre of the rearranged letters
laid out in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A lover of maps is inclined to adopt Henry in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' reworks TOWN and MAPLOVER into WOLVERAMPTON, and 'take ... to heart' puts H at its exact middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolverhampton is a city in the West Midlands of England.

clue.text: He exhibits some uncouth, ugly characteristics

definitions.text: He exhibits some uncouth, ugly characteristics

indicators.note: shows a part of the following words, so the letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: A man displays coarse and unpleasant traits.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent ruffian is just the sort of man to show crude, ugly traits.

clue.text: The acacia pendula means everything to me

parts.note: my is the possessive of me
all means everything

explanation.surface: A gardener says this particular acacia is everything to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The myall is an Australian weeping acacia, botanical name Acacia pendula.

clue.text: Vessel he and I returned to King Edward

indicators.note: turned back, so the pronoun is read from its end

parts.note: the two together are we
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A pot that the speaker and a friend gave back to the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug, a vessel for water.

clue.text: Pacifist imbued with Socialist principles

indicators.note: filled with, so the pacifist's letters hold the socialist inside

parts.note: CO is a conscientious objector, a pacifist
red is a common label for a socialist

explanation.surface: A peace campaigner steeped in left-wing ideals.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs, a person's guiding tenets.

clue.text: Get ready to make an investment

definitions.meaning: invest in the old military sense, to besiege or surround

explanation.surface: Prepare to put money into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' is the siege sense, surrounding a town, not finance.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means be prepared; as one it means surround and attack, which is what investing a town is.

clue.text: He foresees a lot of cash coming to a bank clerk

parts.note: a fortune is a large sum of money
a teller is a cashier in a bank

explanation.surface: A big windfall is heading for someone at the bank counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A clairvoyant predicts people's futures, seeing what lies ahead.

clue.text: Rudiments taught in initial period at school

definitions.text: Rudiments taught in initial period at school

parts.words: Rudiments taught in initial period at school
parts.note: the very first class in a course, where the basics are covered

explanation.surface: The basics learned in the first class of term.
explanation.definitionFit: The first class of a course teaches beginners' basics, and the phrase means the elementary principles.

clue.text: Top price paid for vinyls with little hesitation

parts.note: vinyl discs are records
um is a short sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A collector hesitates briefly before paying a fortune for LPs.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum never exceeded before is the highest amount ever paid.

clue.text: Dance with female relations-but not one's own

parts.note: a step is a dance movement
daughters are female offspring

explanation.surface: Dancing with girls who are family yet not your own children.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's female children from another relationship are kin by marriage, not by birth.

clue.text: Mark one symbol of authority

parts.note: M is short for mark, the old German currency
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A badge of office marked number one.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial staff carried before officials stands for their power.

clue.text: Number one GP in Bordeaux

parts.note: number one is slang for oneself, me
a GP (general practitioner) is a doctor, a doc

explanation.surface: The top family doctor practises in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Medoc is a red wine from the Bordeaux region, so it is one kind of claret.

clue.text: Conservative inclination to be above board

parts.note: a lean is a tilt or slope

explanation.surface: A Tory tendency to be honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest and fair dealing, with nothing hidden, is called clean.

clue.text: Son is going to bivouac, the young rascal

parts.note: to bivouac is to camp out

explanation.surface: A boy heads off camping, the little devil.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous child, a rogue.

clue.text: A pig who's an utter bore

indicators.note: speak out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person

explanation.surface: Someone who is a total pig and a crashing bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like 'complete', but it signals speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is an uncastrated male pig or a wild pig.

clue.text: The way to get in top quality wine

indicators.note: the street letters enter the quality mark

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: Finding a route to the best wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Foot simply admits to being a doctor

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Foot simply admits to being a doctor': I AM + MB gives IAMMB, one M too many, and 'simply' is unexplained; no parse yields IAMB without a word doing two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Foot simply admits to being a doctor

clue.text: Man in parliamentary group gets reduced bill of fare

parts.note: a diet is a parliamentary assembly, as in Japan
a set is a group
he is a man

explanation.surface: A man in a political faction is put on a slimming menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A slimming plan listing permitted foods is a menu of reduced meals.

clue.text: Beers containing nothing laxative

indicators.note: holding inside, so the beers go around the zero

parts.note: ales are beers
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Beers with nothing in them that clear the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter aloes, from the aloe plant, were used as a purgative.

clue.text: State provision

definitions.meaning: a state or ... of health or repair
a stipulation or term in a contract

explanation.surface: A clause describing how things stand.
explanation.definitionFit: It means the state something is in, and also a term laid down in an agreement.

clue.text: Ideal food on Friday for a catholic guitarist

definitions.text: Ideal food on Friday for a catholic
definitions.meaning: Catholics traditionally ate fish rather than meat on Fridays

explanation.surface: A Catholic musician's Friday supper.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a freshwater fish suited to meatless Fridays, and the surname of the guitarist Julian Bream.
